label: rem:qbeta-odd-carrier-hopf-cubic
title: The $\mathfrak{Q}_\beta$ odd-channel obstruction is an irreducible cubic in the trace variable, sourced by the Hopf (double-crossing) sector
html:
Remark. The \mathfrak{Q}_\beta odd-channel obstruction is an irreducible cubic in the trace variable, sourced by the Hopf (double-crossing) sector

Remark (why the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta odd channel resists a real-q closure). The precision-ladder coefficient c_3 splits under the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} into a bar-even part (exactly measured) and a bar-odd part, the latter being the open channel. Its carrier is the bar-odd part of the net decay-width Laurent polynomial \Delta_{\mathrm{net}} = \Delta(\mathfrak{n}) - \Delta(\mathfrak{p}) on the \mathbf{H}_3 normal-form basis, whose numerator over 4q^7 is

\mathrm{num}(q) = q^{14} - 5q^{12} + 10q^{10} - 16q^{8} + 16q^{6} - 10q^{4} + 5q^{2} - 1.

The cyclotomic content factors cleanly into a quantum differential. Exactly, \mathrm{num}(q) = (q^2 - 1)\,R_{12}(q), which means the bar-odd part of the categorical net evaluates exactly to:

\Delta_{\mathrm{net}}^{\mathrm{odd}} = \frac{q - q^{-1}}{4} \cdot C(y) = \frac{h}{4} \cdot C(y)

where h = q - q^{-1} is the quantum differential and C(y) is a cubic in the bar-even loop-trace variable y = q^2 + q^{-2} = 2\cosh 2\lambda given by:

C(y) = y^3 - 4y^2 + 3y - 2.

C is irreducible over \mathbb{Q} (its only possible rational roots \pm 1, \pm 2 are all nonzero), so its root generates a genuine degree-3 field (discriminant -152 = -2^3 \cdot 19, Galois group S_3). Every substrate quadratic anchor sits at a rational trace value — golden \varphi \mapsto y = 3, silver 1 + \sqrt{2} \mapsto y = 6, classical q = 1 \mapsto y = 2 — and C is nonzero at each. A degree-\le 2 number can never be a root of an irreducible cubic, so no quadratic-anchor or real-q construction can reproduce the odd carrier: this is the structural reason the real-q c_3 closures fail.

The degree-3 comes from the Hopf (double-crossing) sector. Decomposing the bar-odd carrier over the knot sectors of the \mathbf{H}_3 normal form isolates the origin of the cubic:

knot sector crossings \Delta^{\mathrm{odd}}_{\mathrm{sector}}
virtual (\sigma_0, \sigma_1) 1 0
trefoil (\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0) 3 0
unknot (\mathbf{1}) 0 \frac{h}{4} \cdot (2y^2 - 7y + 4) = \frac{h}{4} \cdot C_{\mathrm{unknot}}(y)
Hopf (\sigma_0\sigma_1 + \sigma_1\sigma_0) 2 \frac{h}{4} \cdot (y^3 - 6y^2 + 10y - 6) = \frac{h}{4} \cdot C_{\mathrm{Hopf}}(y)

with C = C_{\mathrm{Hopf}} + C_{\mathrm{unknot}}. The odd-crossing sectors (virtual, trefoil) are bar-even and vanish; the identity contributes only a quadratic; the cubic — hence the degree-3 field — is sourced entirely by the Hopf-link (double-crossing) sector. C_{\mathrm{Hopf}} is itself irreducible (discriminant -76 = -2^2 \cdot 19), and the prime 19 is the arithmetic fingerprint shared with the total C. So the obstruction is not a 3-dimensional representation (\mathbf{H}_3 has none — its Wedderburn blocks are 1, 2, 1) nor a single knot invariant, but the two-crossing isospin amplitude difference. Any genuine odd-channel closure must supply the cubic field of C_{\mathrm{Hopf}}, routed through the archimedean evaluation of the Markov crossing term, rather than a fibre-level real-q formula.
